questions.question:
The deployment **legacy-web** in namespace **image-audit** currently runs a known-vulnerable container image. Pre-generated Trivy scan results are stored in ConfigMap **scan-data** in the same namespace.

**Tasks:**
1. Review the scan results in ConfigMap `scan-data`. The safest image is `nginx:1.25-alpine`.
2. Update deployment `legacy-web` to use image `nginx:1.25-alpine`.
3. Add the label `scanned: "true"` to the **pod template** of the deployment.

verification.description: Deployment legacy-web updated to use nginx:1.25-alpine
Pod template of legacy-web has label scanned=true
ConfigMap scan-data exists in namespace image-audit

questions.question:
A Falco custom rule configuration is stored in ConfigMap **falco-custom-rules** in namespace **monitoring** (key: `falco_rules.yaml`). The rule `detect_shell_exec` has priority `NOTICE`.

**Tasks:**
1. Update the rule `detect_shell_exec` priority to `WARNING`.
2. Update the rule output to include `%container.id` and `%user.name` fields.
3. Add a new list named `monitored_shells` with entries: `[bash, sh, ash, zsh, fish]`.

verification.description: Rule detect_shell_exec has priority WARNING in the ConfigMap
Rule output includes container.id and user.name fields
monitored_shells list with 5 entries exists in the ConfigMap

questions.question:
Namespace **three-tier** has three pods: `frontend` (app=frontend, port 80), `backend` (app=backend, port 8080), `db` (app=db, port 5432).

**Tasks - create the following NetworkPolicies:**
1. **backend-isolation**: Ingress to `app=backend` only from `app=frontend` on port 8080. Egress from `app=backend` only to `app=db` on port 5432 and DNS (port 53).
2. **db-isolation**: Ingress to `app=db` only from `app=backend` on port 5432. Deny ALL egress from `app=db`.

Do not restrict frontend traffic.

verification.description: NetworkPolicy backend-isolation exists in namespace three-tier
backend-isolation restricts ingress from app=frontend on port 8080
NetworkPolicy db-isolation restricts ingress from app=backend on port 5432 with no egress

questions.question:
ServiceAccount **dev-sa** in namespace **dev-team** has been granted `cluster-admin` via ClusterRoleBinding **dev-cluster-admin**.

**Tasks:**
1. Delete the ClusterRoleBinding `dev-cluster-admin`.
2. Create Role `dev-role` in namespace `dev-team` allowing **get, list, watch** on: `pods`, `services`, `deployments`.
3. Create RoleBinding `dev-role-binding` in namespace `dev-team` binding `dev-role` to ServiceAccount `dev-sa`.

verification.description: ClusterRoleBinding dev-cluster-admin has been deleted
Role dev-role exists with correct get/list/watch on pods, services, deployments
RoleBinding dev-role-binding binds dev-role to dev-sa

questions.question:
Verifying the integrity of cluster binaries is a CKS security requirement.

**Tasks:**
1. Create Pod `hash-checker` in namespace **binary-verification** using image `busybox:1.35` that:
   - Mounts host path `/usr/local/bin` read-only at `/host-bin` via `hostPath` volume
   - Command: `sh -c "sha256sum /host-bin/kubectl | tee /tmp/hash.txt; sleep 3600"`
   - `restartPolicy: OnFailure`
2. Create ConfigMap `verification-info` with: `binary_path: /usr/local/bin/kubectl`, `verification_method: sha256sum`, `status: verified`.

verification.description: Pod hash-checker exists with hostPath volume mounting /usr/local/bin at /host-bin
Pod hash-checker command includes sha256sum
ConfigMap verification-info exists with required fields

questions.question:
Configure the cluster to encrypt Secrets at rest.

**Tasks:**
1. Create ConfigMap `encryption-config` in `kube-system` with key `encryption.yaml` containing a valid `EncryptionConfiguration` (apiVersion: `apiserver.config.k8s.io/v1`) that:
   - Sets `resources: [secrets]`
   - Uses `aescbc` as the first provider with a base64-encoded 32-byte key named `key1`
   - Includes `identity: {}` as the fallback (second) provider
2. Create Secret `encryption-test` in `kube-system` with `data.test-key: dGVzdA==`.

verification.description: ConfigMap encryption-config exists in kube-system with key encryption.yaml
encryption.yaml contains aescbc provider with a key
encryption.yaml includes identity fallback provider
Secret encryption-test exists in kube-system

questions.question:
Document a Kyverno ClusterPolicy to enforce security labeling of all pods.

**Tasks:**
1. Create ConfigMap `security-policy` in namespace **policy-config** with key `policy.yaml` containing a Kyverno `ClusterPolicy` YAML that:
   - Name: `require-security-label`
   - Rule named `check-security-scan-label` validating pods have label `security-scan: completed`
   - Validation action: `Audit`
2. Create ConfigMap `policy-exceptions` with: `exempt_namespaces: kube-system,monitoring,cert-manager` and `policy_name: require-security-label`.

verification.description: ConfigMap security-policy exists in namespace policy-config with key policy.yaml
policy.yaml contains ClusterPolicy with rule check-security-scan-label
ConfigMap policy-exceptions exists with exempt_namespaces field

questions.question:
Namespace **legacy-workloads** has a deployment **privileged-app** that violates Pod Security Standards.

**Tasks:**
1. Apply label `pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: baseline` to namespace `legacy-workloads`.
2. Fix deployment `privileged-app` by removing `privileged: true` and `hostPID: true`, and setting `runAsNonRoot: true`.
3. Create Pod `baseline-compliant` using image `nginx:1.25-alpine` that complies with baseline PSS.

verification.description: Namespace legacy-workloads has enforce=baseline label
Deployment privileged-app has privileged=false and hostPID=false
Pod baseline-compliant exists and is Running

**Tasks:**
1. Create ConfigMap `image-webhook-config` in `kube-system` with key `admission_config.yaml` containing a valid `ImagePolicyWebhook` AdmissionConfiguration with `defaultAllow: false`, `allowTTL: 50`, `denyTTL: 50`.
2. Create ConfigMap `allowed-registries` in `kube-system` with `registries: registry.k8s.io,docker.io/library,gcr.io`.

admission_config.yaml contains defaultAllow: false

questions.question:
Namespace **web-tls** has a pre-deployed Service `web-service` (port 80). A TLS certificate and key are in ConfigMap `raw-certs` (keys: `tls.crt` and `tls.key`).

**Tasks:**
1. Create TLS Secret `web-tls-secret` in namespace `web-tls` from the cert data in ConfigMap `raw-certs`.
2. Create Ingress `web-ingress` with:
   - Host: `app.cks-exam.io`, Backend: `web-service:80`
   - TLS section using `web-tls-secret` for host `app.cks-exam.io`
   - Annotation: `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/ssl-redirect: "true"`

verification.description: TLS Secret web-tls-secret exists in web-tls with tls.crt and tls.key
Ingress web-ingress exists in namespace web-tls
Ingress has TLS for host app.cks-exam.io using web-tls-secret
Ingress routes to web-service backend on port 80

questions.question:
Deployment **data-processor** in namespace **mutable-apps** runs with a mutable filesystem, root user, and allows privilege escalation.

**Tasks - patch deployment `data-processor`:**
1. Set `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true` on the container.
2. Set `runAsUser: 1000` and `runAsNonRoot: true` on the container.
3. Set `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false` on the container.
4. Add `emptyDir` volume `tmp-dir` mounted at `/tmp`.

verification.description: data-processor has readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
data-processor runs as user 1000 with runAsNonRoot: true
data-processor has allowPrivilegeEscalation: false and emptyDir at /tmp

questions.question:
Workloads in namespace **cloud-workloads** must not access the cloud metadata service at `169.254.169.254` (IMDS endpoint used in SSRF attacks to steal cloud credentials).

**Tasks:**
1. Create NetworkPolicy `block-metadata` in `cloud-workloads` applying to all pods that denies egress to `169.254.169.254/32` while allowing all other egress.
2. Create Pod `cloud-app` using image `busybox:1.35`, command `sleep 3600`, label `app=cloud-app`.

verification.description: NetworkPolicy block-metadata exists in cloud-workloads
NetworkPolicy blocks egress to 169.254.169.254/32
Pod cloud-app exists in cloud-workloads

questions.question:
Deployment **legacy-app** in namespace **workload-ns** uses the `default` ServiceAccount with `automountServiceAccountToken: true`, granting unnecessary API access.

**Tasks:**
1. Create ServiceAccount `minimal-sa` in `workload-ns` with `automountServiceAccountToken: false`.
2. Create Role `minimal-role` in `workload-ns` allowing only `get` and `list` on `pods`.
3. Create RoleBinding `minimal-binding` binding `minimal-role` to `minimal-sa`.
4. Update deployment `legacy-app` to use `minimal-sa` as serviceAccountName with `automountServiceAccountToken: false` in pod spec.

verification.description: ServiceAccount minimal-sa exists with automountServiceAccountToken: false
Role minimal-role exists with only get/list on pods
Deployment legacy-app uses minimal-sa with automountServiceAccountToken: false

questions.question:
Namespace **cert-monitoring** has TLS Secret `monitor-cert`. Create a pod that validates the certificate expiry.

**Tasks:**
1. Create Pod `cert-validator` using image `alpine:3.18` that:
   - Mounts Secret `monitor-cert` at `/etc/tls` (read-only)
   - Command: `sh -c "apk add --no-cache openssl && openssl x509 -in /etc/tls/tls.crt -noout -enddate > /tmp/expiry.txt && sleep 3600"`
   - Label `app=cert-validator`
2. Create ConfigMap `cert-info` with: `certName: monitor-cert`, `namespace: cert-monitoring`, `checkType: expiry`.

verification.description: Pod cert-validator exists and mounts monitor-cert at /etc/tls
Pod cert-validator uses openssl in its command
ConfigMap cert-info exists with certName and checkType fields
